workflow: A stateful iterator reads a child object and invokes user-controlled iteration while retaining only a borrowed reference to that child.
The child re-enters the same outer iterator before the original retrieval finishes.
The re-entrant call exhausts or removes the child and releases its storage.
The original retrieval resumes and dereferences the retained pointer as though the child were still alive.
The access reaches freed memory and terminates the process instead of rejecting re-entrant execution.
summary: Reentrant iteration releases a child object still used by the outer retrieval
decision_reason: The failure workflow materially matches reentrant mutation of shared iterator state: user code runs during an in-progress operation, re-enters the same container-like object, releases state held by the outer operation, and the outer operation then uses invalidated storage.
